sequences.subject: {{company}} shouldn't hear about it from a permit pull
sequences.email_body:
{{first_name}} — you build $2M customs. You shouldn't be finding out about the next one from a permit pull everyone else in {{county}} sees the same day you do.

Proof I'm not guessing: {{company}} pulled {{trigger_event_detail}} in {{county}} last month. By the time that's public, the architect already named two builders to the client — and you weren't one of them. Not because you're not the better builder. Because you were late.

You didn't build the name in this market to wait on Houzz leads.

Worth showing you the projects forming around you before the rest of {{state}} sees them?

— Ethan, ContractMotion

sequences.subject: The builder named before the meeting wins it
sequences.email_body:
{{first_name}} — the builders closing $800k–$2M+ without bidding against four other names aren't better closers. They're earlier.

They're in the buyer's head before any other builder gets a call — through the architect, not a directory. You've already got the reputation that earns that introduction. What you don't have is anything that travels into the room ahead of you: a portfolio, build-process photography, a leave-behind that answers "why this builder" before you shake a hand.

This is built for builders closing $1.5M+ customs, not spec-flippers.

Want to see what the room sees before you walk in?

— Ethan, ContractMotion

sequences.subject: The $30k you're leaking on change orders
sequences.email_body:
{{first_name}} — one thing the market leaders fixed early, before I move on.

A single change-order dispute runs $18–40k in legal and lost margin. They're the #1 source of mechanics liens in residential — we watch them hit CourtListener across {{state}} every week. Same story every time: texts instead of signatures, a verbal yes that vanishes when the invoice lands.

A builder at {{company}}'s level shouldn't be financing a homeowner's memory. The presales stack that gets your name in front of architects also locks down the paper that kills those disputes — portfolio, build-process photography, case-study leave-behind, built in 30 days.

Send the sample deck?

— Ethan, ContractMotion

sequences.subject: Closing your file, {{first_name}}
sequences.email_body:
{{first_name}} — I've sent a few notes about getting {{company}} in the room before the rest of {{county}} hears the project exists. No reply, so I'll close the file.

When we put a builder's name on projects forming in their market, we tie our fee to the work it lands — you don't pay for a map that goes nowhere. If owning your market beats competing in it, the door's open.

Either way, good luck out there — you've clearly built something worth protecting.

— Ethan, ContractMotion
